lesson_title: Headlights, Speedometer, Mirror: Reading the Economy's Dashboard
hook_text: Unemployment can't predict a recovery. Building plans can. Here's the trick to sorting every indicator in seconds.
clip_script: Picture the economy as a taxi on the N1 at night. Headlights show what's COMING: building plans passed, job adverts, factory orders. Nobody passes a building plan for fun — someone intends to build next year. Those are leading indicators. The speedometer shows NOW: retail tills ringing, factories producing, GDP itself. Coincident. And the rear-view mirror shows where you've BEEN — and here's the one everyone gets wrong: jobs are the mirror. Think like a boss. Business turns bad — you delay retrenching, hoping it passes. Business turns good — you delay hiring, until you're sure. Jobs move LAST. By the time unemployment falls, the recovery is old news. Now check the passengers, because a fast taxi with sick passengers is going nowhere good. How long do people live? Do babies reach their first birthday? Do the taps and lights work? And the sharpest question of all — the Gini: however much money the taxi carries, how is it SHARED? Zero means equally. One means a single passenger holds everything. South Africa scores 0,63 — near the top of the world's unfairness table. One taxi. Every indicator sorted. That's the whole dashboard.
visual_style: A minibus taxi on a dark highway — headlights sweeping over icons of cranes and job ads, a glowing speedometer of tills and factories, a mirror reflecting a queue outside a factory gate; then the interior lights up passenger by passenger as the gauges appear.
pacing: Three clean beats for headlights, speedo, mirror; a reflective slow-down for the passengers; a hard landing on the Gini number.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any indicator — economic or social — like it's your own dashboard.
